text:
ashley: Heads-up — we need to decide region commitments for H2 inference fleet before EOD Fri. Running a cost/latency comparison across us-west1, europe-west2, asia-east1. Spreadsheet: https://redwood-sheets.internal/s/commitment-plan (view only). Key constraints: customer latency SLOs for EUAP, egress costs, and 1yr vs 3yr commitment tradeoffs.

vikram: I put together a quick cost table in the sheet. High-level numbers (per-GPU effective hourly):
- us-west1: on-demand 0.90/hr, spot ~0.25/hr, 1yr reserved ~0.60/hr, 3yr reserved ~0.45/hr
- europe-west2: on-demand 1.10/hr, spot ~0.35/hr, 1yr reserved ~0.75/hr, 3yr reserved ~0.65/hr
- asia-east1: on-demand 1.30/hr, spot ~0.40/hr, 1yr reserved ~0.90/hr, 3yr reserved ~0.70/hr
Also added egress: us->eu ~0.09/GB, eu->us ~0.08/GB, asia egress slightly higher. Numbers in sheet cells B12:E20.

stef: Noted. For production latency: EU users need p95 <80ms. Routing EU traffic to us-west1 breaks that. So we need a local hot pool in europe-west2 (small footprint) to hit SLOs, even if it's slightly more expensive. Cold pools / batch can be elsewhere.

samir: Proposal: hybrid commit
- 60% of baseline capacity in us-west1 on 3yr reserved (best unit cost)
- 30% in europe-west2 on 1yr reserved to keep some flexibility for EU demand growth
- 10% in asia as on-demand/spot for burst (monitor 90d and decide)
This splits risk and leaves room for re-up after 1yr.

maria: A couple of finance notes: cloud providers give better accelerator discounts for multi-year commitments and larger volumes — we should negotiate enterprise pricing if we commit >200 GPUs regionally. Also check whether commitments are per-project or per-billing-account; mixing projects can leak discounts. I asked finance to run scenario PV for 1yr vs 3yr with our growth curve.

ashley: Can we get a quick break-even calc for 3yr vs on-demand assuming 70% utilization? Need to justify capital lock.

vikram: Quick calc (back-of-envelope):
```
unit_on_demand = 0.90  # us-west1
unit_3yr = 0.45
util = 0.7
cost_on_demand_per_hour = unit_on_demand * util
cost_3yr_per_hour = unit_3yr * util
savings_per_gpu_per_hour = cost_on_demand_per_hour - cost_3yr_per_hour
savings_per_gpu_per_month ≈ savings_per_gpu_per_hour * 24 * 30
# plug numbers: (0.9-0.45)*0.7*24*30 ≈ $226/month per GPU
```
So ~226 USD/mo per GPU at 70% util in us-west1. Multiply by GPUs committed gives payback.

stef: Remember to include egress/replication overhead — EU traffic routed locally avoids egress but increases local infra costs. For cross-region model sync we have ~0.12 TB/day per model version push; factor that into first-month delta.

maria: Also flag on contract flexibility: some reserved commitments allow partial region re-assignment within the same billing account. That might let us shift unused capacity between us and eu without full penalty. I'll get exact policy.

ashley: If we go hybrid, what's the operational burden? Can we autoscale across regions and fall back to cheaper pools if capacity hits 95%?

samir: Yes — routing policy can prefer local pools, then failover to regional cheaper pools with model-variant fallback. But we need confirmed cross-region latency for failover and throttling rules. Ops work: add a canary and failover playbook, + alerting for cross-region fallbacks.

vikram: Updated the sheet with a 3-scenario summary: conservative (1yr EU heavy), aggressive (3yr US heavy), hybrid (samir's). See tab 'scenarios'. I added a short terraform snippet to pin zones in the hybrid plan for testing: 
```
resource "google_compute_instance" "inference_gpu" {
  count = var.gpu_count
  zone  = "${var.region == \"eu\" ? \"europe-west2-a\" : \"us-west1-a\"}"
  machine_type = "n1-standard-16"
  guest_accelerator {
    type  = "nvidia-tesla-h100"
    count = 1
  }
}
```

ashley: Good. Next steps: Maria/Finance to confirm negotiation thresholds and commitment flexibility by Wed. Vikram to run projected utilization sensitivity (60/70/80%) and paste numbers in sheet. Stef/Ops to draft failover runbook and add SLO test. Samir to model risk (commit mismatch) and propose a buyback/transfer plan.

maria: Will do. If we can squeeze a 5-8% additional discount by committing 250+ GPUs in aggregate we should consider shifting a small chunk from EU 1yr -> US 3yr and then use regional reserved flex if policy allows.

billing-bot: Monthly billing export uploaded: https://redwood-billing.internal/exports/2026-02.csv (triggered 1762000889).

ashley: OK — thanks everyone. If no major objections I'll publish the hybrid recommendation and set a 48h window for pushback before starting procurement. :thumbsup:

vikram: :thumbsup: I'll also add a sensitivity chart and small note on spot eviction risk and preemption budget.

stef: +1 — will start runbook template.

samir: +1

maria: +1
